display.purpose: The count on Check the list, and nothing else. 40px on a phone.

headline.purpose: A screen's title (Home, Photos, Tools). 28px on a phone.

figure.purpose: Home's four facts, in tabular numerals. 28px on a phone.

title.purpose: A tool's name over its form, a group's name on the Tools page; the counters under What happened at 700.

section.purpose: Home's section heads, Latest, a month on Photos; the verb and unit beside the count.

masthead.purpose: The app's name in the header: wide, heavy, small.

subtitle.purpose: A card's heading and the group's name over the list beside a tool; a tool's name in a list at 650.

body.purpose: Everything that is read. Lines under titles stop at 62ch.

small.purpose: Secondary lines, chips, steps, tables, header controls.

label.purpose: Running heads in the rail and the list beside a tool, in sentence case.

caption.purpose: A plate's file name and date; table headers at 600.

shadows.name: shadow-card
shadows.purpose: Every flat surface. A card sits on the page by its hairline alone.

shadows.name: shadow-pop (light)
shadows.purpose: Menus, the selection bar, anything that floats over the page.

shadows.name: running-head (light)
shadows.purpose: The header, only once the page has scrolled under it.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Every catalogue movement: arrives quickly, settles slowly, never bounces.

motion.name: t-fast
motion.purpose: Colour, border and fill changes on controls; the skip link dropping in.

motion.name: t-mid
motion.purpose: The turn between screens; photo tiles fading in; colour of a step.

motion.name: t-slow
motion.purpose: The lit step filling in, plates rising, the count settling.

motion.name: turn
motion.value: pm-turn: opacity 0 to 1, translateX(18px) to none, var(--t-mid) var(--ease); back from -18px; later parts 40ms apart up to 120ms
motion.purpose: Arriving on a screen or a tool. Not on a redraw in place.

motion.name: plates
motion.value: pm-plate: opacity 0 to 1, translateY(10px) to none, var(--t-slow) var(--ease); 30ms apart
motion.purpose: Home plates laid out one after another.

motion.name: settle
motion.value: pm-settle: opacity 0 to 1, translateY(14px) and letter-spacing .02em to none, var(--t-slow) var(--ease)
motion.purpose: The count on Check the list.

motion.name: lit-step
motion.value: transform: scaleX(0) to scaleX(1), origin left, var(--t-slow) var(--ease)
motion.purpose: The rule under the step you are on.

motion.name: tiles
motion.value: pm-fade: opacity 0 to 1, var(--t-mid) ease-out; 30ms steps
motion.purpose: The photo grid, quicker than the plates because there are hundreds.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: None at all for anybody who asked the machine for less. The last rule in page/style.css.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: Rail becomes a drawer, tabs at the foot, 16px gutters, 44px targets, plates swiped.

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Plates go to three columns; the list beside a tool moves under the form.

narrative.overview:
Photo Manager is set like a museum photography catalogue. The photographs are the plates, and everything else is set around them in one typeface, on one type scale, divided by hairline rules, with each section of tools opened by a band of its own ink. The default stock is black: a near-black ground, a sheet a half step lighter, bone ink, and a warm grey for the quieter line. In light mode the same page is printed on white stock in black ink.

Density follows the job. Home and Photos give the plates the room, tool pages and Settings are a column of ruled rows with space between them, and the list a run is about to apply reads as a catalogue checklist with its count at plate size. Colour is rationed. Apart from the photographs, the only colour in the chrome is the ink of the section you are in, one of five, one per group of tools. The primary action is printed in the page's own ink.

The system refuses the category default of grey cards nested in cards, pastel figure tiles, rounded everything and one blue accent. Motion is a page being turned and laid flat: quick to arrive, slow to settle, never a bounce, and nothing at all for anybody who has asked the machine for less.
keyCharacteristics: Black catalogue stock by default and white stock in light mode, in one warm neutral family.
One variable typeface, Archivo, served by the app itself, on eight sizes and nothing between.
Every surface, control and chip cut square at 2px.
Hairlines and ink rules instead of boxes and shadows.
Five section inks, used only to say which group of tools something belongs to.
Every count in tabular numerals, and the count you approve set at 64px.
Screens turn like spreads in 280ms, and stand still under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Printed Ink Rule
rules.body: The primary action is printed in the page's own ink, bone on black and black on white. There is no brand colour; the blue-grey look before 4.0 is the Original theme with the Blue accent under Appearance, and the other palettes, accents and frames there are the viewer's choices, not this system.

rules.name: The Section Ink Rule
rules.body: A section ink says which group of tools something belongs to, and nothing else. Home, Photos, Places, Albums and People are in no section, so their own chrome is ink only.

rules.name: The 4.5 Rule
rules.body: Every section ink reads at 4.5:1 or better as text on the ground and on the card, in both modes. `tests/test_design.py` holds it, so a new ink is checked before it ships.

rules.name: The Never By Colour Alone Rule
rules.body: A state is said in shape and word as well as hue: the step you are on is bold and lit, a finished step has a drawn tick, a status dot is a hollow ring when off and filled when on with its word beside it, and a run that cannot be undone is banded, headed with a warning mark and counted in red.

rules.name: The Eight Sizes Rule
rules.body: Every size is one of 12, 13, 14, 16, 20, 28, 40 and 64px (`--t-xs` to `--t-4xl`). A size off the scale is a size somebody guessed, and `tests/test_design.py` fails it.

rules.name: The Columned Numbers Rule
rules.body: Every count is set in tabular numerals, so a column of 1,204 and 87 reads as numbers and not as a ragged edge.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings, legends, fold rows and running heads are in sentence case. A running head is small and spaced, never capitals, and nothing sits above a heading: the line about a screen goes under its title.

rules.name: The Plates First Rule
rules.body: On Home the newest photos come before any figure: the newest at twice the size, a wall label under every plate, and the four facts after them.

rules.name: The Answer Width Rule
rules.body: A field is as wide as what goes in it. A box for "60" stretched across a wide column reads as a mistake.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: A card sits on the page by its hairline alone. Nothing flat casts a shadow; only a menu, a bar or a bubble that floats over the page does.

rules.name: The Band, Not Stripe Rule
rules.body: A section or a state is banded across the top: a 4px band, a 3px lit step, a 2px band on a phone tab. Nothing carries a coloured stripe down one side; a 1px hairline between two columns is a divider, not a stripe, and `tests/test_design.py` fails any left border of 2px or more.

rules.name: The Square Cut Rule
rules.body: 2px on every card, control and chip. What sets a control apart is its fill, its weight or its rule, never its roundness.

rules.name: The Six Roles Rule
rules.body: Every button is one of primary, secondary, quiet, destructive, filter or contextual. A seventh kind is a feature that has not said which of these it means, and `tests/test_design.py` fails a new one.

dos: **Do** print the one primary action on a screen in ink (`accent` with `on-accent`), and name it with its verb and count ("Move 412 files").
**Do** take every size from the scale (`--t-xs` 12px to `--t-4xl` 64px) and set every count in tabular numerals.
**Do** divide with 1px hairlines (`line`), open a printed section with a 1px ink rule, and open a section of the catalogue with a 4px band of its ink.
**Do** reach a section ink only through `--sec` (from `body[data-tone]`) or a group's own `--tone`, and only on something that belongs to a group of tools.
**Do** keep every corner at 2px (`--r-card`, `--r-ctl`, `--r-pill`) and keep round for dots.
**Do** keep everything a thumb presses at 44px or more on a phone (`--chip-h` is 44px under 860px).
**Do** say a state in shape and word as well as colour: bold and lit for the current step, a drawn tick for a finished one, a ring or a filled dot with its word for a status.
**Do** draw every mark (close, arrow, fold, chevron) from the icon sprite or in CSS, at 14px beside text.
**Do** time motion with `--ease` and `--t-fast` (160ms), `--t-mid` (280ms) or `--t-slow` (480ms), and stop all of it under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** set headings in sentence case, with any line about them underneath.
donts: **Don't** build the category default: grey cards nested in cards, pastel figure tiles, rounded everything, one blue accent.
**Don't** box a group of settings inside a card; a group is a heading and a rule.
**Don't** run a coloured stripe down the side of anything; a left border of 2px or more fails `tests/test_design.py`.
**Don't** colour the chrome of a screen that is in no section (Home, Photos, Places, Albums, People) with a section ink, or use a section ink as decoration.
**Don't** cast a shadow from a flat surface, or let the header turn see-through.
**Don't** add a seventh button role, or a second primary button on a screen.
**Don't** add a type size off the scale, a second typeface, or a font or script fetched from the internet.
**Don't** put a kicker or an eyebrow above a heading, or set a heading in capitals.
**Don't** type a mark as a character (× ‹ › ▾ ▸ ↑ ↓).
**Don't** bounce, and don't loop anything but the pulse of a running status dot or a progress bar that cannot measure.
